parameterInfo.cylinderTotal: Sum of anterior and posterior corneal surface astigmatism.
parameterInfo.axisTotal: True orientation of corneal astigmatism, considering both anterior and posterior corneal surfaces.
parameterInfo.offsetLimbus: Distance between the geometric center of the limbus and the center of the pupil. Clinically relevant values: > 0.75 mm.
parameterInfo.offsetPupil: Distance between the pupil center and the corneal optical center/visual axis (related to angle kappa or chord mu). Clinically relevant values: > 0.50 mm.
parameterInfo.sri: Surface Regularity Index: average curvature differences between neighboring points in the central cornea, quantifying local regularity. No universal formula exists; each topographer uses different interpolation, smoothing, and weighting. Clinically relevant values: > 0.70.
parameterInfo.sai: Surface Asymmetry Index: average curvature differences between opposite points, measuring asymmetry of the corneal surface around the central axis. Clinically relevant values: > 0.50.
parameterInfo.cornealSa: Corneal spherical aberration: aberration caused by different refraction of peripheral versus central rays. It interacts with IOL design and can reduce contrast and visual quality, especially in mesopic/scotopic conditions. Clinically relevant values for a 4 mm pupil: < -0.20 or > 0.25 µ.
parameterInfo.cornealComa: Corneal coma: aberration caused by corneal asymmetry, producing distorted and elongated images. It is a major cause of reduced non-correctable visual quality. Clinically relevant values for a 4 mm pupil: > 0.20 µ.
parameterInfo.cornealHoa: Corneal higher-order aberrations: imperfections of the corneal surface that distort image quality. Clinically relevant values for a 4 mm pupil: > 0.20 µ.
parameterInfo.pupilPhotopic: Pupil diameter determines how much of the IOL optic is used and is a key factor in photic phenomena and postoperative visual quality. Clinically relevant values: > 4.5 mm.
parameterInfo.pupilMesopic: Pupil diameter determines how much of the IOL optic is used and is a key factor in photic phenomena and postoperative visual quality. Clinically relevant values: > 5.5 mm.
parameterInfo.pupilScotopic: Pupil diameter determines how much of the IOL optic is used and is a key factor in photic phenomena and postoperative visual quality. Clinically relevant values: > 6.0 mm.
parameterInfo.axialLength: Axial Length: influences calculation predictability, risk of IOL decentration/tilt, and visual quality. Clinically relevant values: < 21 mm or > 26.0 mm.
parameterInfo.acDepth: One of the main factors in estimating final IOL position, and therefore refractive precision and postoperative visual quality. Clinically relevant values: < 2.0 mm or > 4.5 mm.
parameterInfo.lensThickness: Lens Thickness: does not directly affect IOL optics, but affects effective lens position (ELP), stability, refractive outcome, and final visual quality. Clinically relevant values: > 5.0 mm.
